newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse's blue chip stocks gain ground.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse's blue chip stocks gain ground.

text.p: The Casablanca stock market closed 0.73 percent higher on Thursday with leading stocks building on yesterday's gains, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 514.09 from 510.36 points on Wednesday.
"There is a shortage of shares and too many buyers. We need new flotations," a broker at BMCI Securities said.
ONA group the first biggest holding, remained unchanged at 635 dirhams.
Upline Securities said in a recent report that ONA net earnings are expected to reach 852 million dirhams ($92.6 million) in 1996 from 602 million in 1995.

Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate, which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, was up seven dirhams at 598 dirhams. The conglomerate has a market capitalisation of more than 5.6 billion dirhams.

Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique closed unchanged at 180 dirhams. Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie gained two to 382 dirhams. Wafabank leapt to 688 dirhams, up 20. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, a blue chip stock, rose 13 dirhams to trade at 472 dirhams.
Samir oil refinery, the country's main refinery, gained six to close at 271 dirhams. Societe Cherifienne des Petroles rose 15 to 600.
Newly-floated Credor advanced seven dirhams to 600 dirhams.
Volume on the official market was 81.3 million dirhams against 75.5 million during the previous session.
